title: Salary Survey Australia: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Use our salary survey Australia guide to convert hourly pay to annual salary. Includes 38-hour week, fortnight, tax, super, and minimum wage rates.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52; the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1004.90 per week).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, $30 per hour gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime. Use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our calculator, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% to your base rate – do not enter a rate that already includes loading. See [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for more.

faqs.q: How much tax and super will I pay on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator for a detailed breakdown.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: From Hourly to Annual

When you look at a **salary survey australia**, you’ll often see annual figures, but many jobs pay by the hour. Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary helps you compare offers, budget, and understand your tax and super obligations. This guide explains the simple maths, the key pay rates set by the Fair Work Commission, and what to expect from the Australian Taxation Office.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a full-time employee working the standard 38-hour week, the formula is:

**Annual = hourly × 38 × 52**

For example, if you earn $30 per hour:
$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year.

If you work part-time or casual hours, use your actual weekly hours. A fortnightly figure is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two – useful if you’re paid every two weeks.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1004.90 per week** for 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement.

Most employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. Award rates vary by classification and can include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay Calculator to find the correct award rate for your job.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees get a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (sick leave, annual leave). The casual National Minimum Wage is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our calculator, tick the “casual loading” checkbox – never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

### Superannuation (Super) Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee of **12%** of your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. This is not deducted from your salary – it’s an additional contribution. The super guarantee applies up to a maximum contribution base of **$270,830** per year. For example, on a $59,280 salary, your employer would add $7,113.60 in super ($59,280 × 0.12).

### Tax and Medicare Levy

For the 2026–27 income year, the Australian Taxation Office applies these resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001 and over: 45%

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (generally). The tax-free threshold of $18,200 means you pay no tax on the first $18,200 of income. Our estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed.

### Average Weekly Earnings (ABS)

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports **Average Weekly Earnings** for May 2026:
- Full-time adult ordinary time: **$2,083.70 per week**
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): **$1,579.20 per week**

These figures help you benchmark your pay against the national average. A **salary survey australia** often uses ABS data to show typical pay by industry and occupation.

### Using Our Calculator

[The timesheet](/) lets you enter your hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading. The results include an estimate of tax, Medicare, and super (paid on top). Remember: this is an estimate, not a determination. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

For more detail on minimum pay, visit our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. To explore award rates and pay guides, see [pay guides](/blog). For a full breakdown of tax and super, check [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time).
- National Minimum Wage: $26.44/hr, casual $33.05/hr.
- Super is 12% on top, up to $270,830.
- Tax brackets start at nil for the first $18,200.
- Use a **salary survey australia** to compare your rate with industry benchmarks.

Whether you’re negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, understanding the conversion from hourly to annual helps you make informed decisions.
